a key issue in the implementation of the WFD: How to prioritize streams for management actions.
the selection of streams for RBMPs, which is an issue of high importance in the WFD.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the selection of streams for RBMP can be based on stream slope, width and planform, and that the probability of reaching good ecological status increases with increasing slope, width and sinuosity, but that a threshold value for these parameters can be identified, above which the probability of achieving minimum good status is high enough to justify the selection of streams.
Danish streams with a slope < 0.8%, a width < 2.5 m, and a sinuosity < 1.5 have a low probability of achieving minimum good status and should therefore not be included in future RBMPs.
the Danish headwater streams are generally too small to support a biota of high quality, as required by the WFD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Danish headwater streams have a potential to achieve good ecological status.

the probability for achieving minimum good ecological quality in headwater streams increases with stream slope, width and DHI, whereas the sinuosity has a negative effect on the probability for achieving good ecological status.

the Danish WFD stream monitoring program is well suited to provide a basis for prioritization of headwater streams in the RBMP, and that the obtained results provide clear and sound scientific support for this prioritization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the selection of headwaters streams for the next WFD cycle can be based on a scientifically sound and analytically based process.
headwater streams can be prioritized for RBMPs based on a combination of physical and biological criteria.

the selection of headwaters for the next generation WFD RBMP can benefit greatly from a scientifically based and transparent selection process, where a combination of physical habitat and biological criteria are considered.
